correctness.rationale: An n-spoke leaf-cover lower bound forces exactly n selected vertices, one per spoke; hub domination forbids the empty rim choice. The possible adjacent slides are single spoke toggles. Hamming geodesic obstructions occur precisely when disjoint independent sets are completely cross-adjacent; a C_n with n>=5 has no K2,2, leaving n adjacent-singleton and n singleton-versus-two-neighbor cases. Parity proves +2 is minimal, and explicit 4-/5-move detours attain it. Gaps between selected rim sites give exact maximum disjoint independent sets, eccentricities, radii and diameters, with n=3,4 handled separately. Independent exhaustive original-helm checks n<=8 and all-pairs BFS n<=13 confirm finite instances, without replacing the general proof.

value.rationale: The count 2n of exactly disrupted origin-destination pairs and the sharp +2 worst-case detour are natural exact one-router-failure metrics for a canonical Lucas cube; the helm independent-domination interpretation ties this routing problem to a natural optimal-solution reconfiguration model. The all-size metric, radius, diameter and antipodes make the result reusable for exact routing/reconfiguration benchmarks, not an arbitrary small-graph table.
